stories.headline: Thinking Machines Unveils 'Interaction Models' for Real-Time Audio/Video AI

key_facts.fact: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab announced a research preview of 'interaction models' on May 11, 2026 — a new class of natively multimodal AI that processes audio, video and text in continuous 200ms micro-turns, listening, watching and responding simultaneously instead of in turn-taking style.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're announcing a research preview of interaction models: models that handle interaction natively rather than through external scaffolding... they continuously take in audio, video, and text, and think, respond, and act in real time.

key_facts.fact: The lead system, TML-Interaction-Small, is a 276-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 12B active parameters, paired with a separate deeper-reasoning module to handle slower thinking.
key_facts.excerpt: The research preview introduces TML-Interaction-Small, a 276-billion parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 12 billion active parameters.

key_facts.fact: On the FD-bench interaction benchmark, the model reports a turn-taking latency of 0.40 seconds vs. 0.57s for Gemini-3.1-flash-live and 1.18s for GPT-realtime-2.0 (minimal).
key_facts.excerpt: Responsiveness: It achieved a turn-taking latency of 0.40 seconds, compared to 0.57s for Gemini-3.1-flash-live and 1.18s for GPT-realtime-2.0 (minimal).

key_facts.fact: Thinking Machines will open a limited research preview to collect feedback in the coming months and plans a wider release later this year; the model is not yet publicly available.
key_facts.excerpt: Thinking Machines plans to open a 'limited research preview' in the 'coming months' and aims to do a 'wider release later this year.'

key_facts.fact: Demos showed the model backchanneling during human speech, translating speech live, noticing a user slouching, and flagging an animal mentioned in a story.
key_facts.excerpt: Thinking Machines also shared several examples of the model in action, including listening for mentions of animals in a story, translating speech in real time, and telling someone when they're slouching.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches $4B Deployment Company, Acquires Consulting Firm Tomoro

key_facts.fact: OpenAI on May 11, 2026 launched 'OpenAI Deployment Company,' a majority-owned and -controlled new entity to help large enterprises build and deploy AI, capitalised with more than $4 billion of initial investment from a consortium of 19 investment firms, consultancies and system integrators.
key_facts.excerpt: It will launch with more than $4 billion of initial investment, which it will use to scale operations and acquire firms that can accelerate our mission of ensuring that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

key_facts.fact: TPG is leading the consortium, with Advent International, Bain Capital and Brookfield as co-lead founding partners; Goldman Sachs, SoftBank Corp., Warburg Pincus and BBVA also participate.
key_facts.excerpt: TPG is leading the investment, with Advent, Bain Capital, and Brookfield as co-lead founding partners. Goldman Sachs, SoftBank Corp., Warburg Pincus, and BBVA are also involved.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the launch, OpenAI agreed to acquire Tomoro, a London-based applied AI consultancy founded in 2023, bringing roughly 150 Forward Deployed Engineers and Deployment Specialists into the new entity from day one. Tomoro's clients include Tesco, Virgin Atlantic, Mattel, Red Bull and Supercell.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has agreed to acquire Tomoro, giving the OpenAI Deployment Company experienced Forward Deployed Engineers from day one... The acquisition will bring approximately 150 experienced Forward Deployed Engineers and Deployment Specialists to the OpenAI Deployment Company from day one.

key_facts.fact: The Tomoro acquisition price was not disclosed and is expected to close in the coming months, subject to regulatory approvals.
key_facts.excerpt: The Tomoro acquisition price has not been disclosed... the deal closes in the second half of 2026.

key_facts.fact: Industry analysts cited estimate Deployment Company could eventually reach 2,000 to 4,000 deployment engineers within three years, supporting a multi-billion-dollar annual run rate before customer revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: Industry analysts have estimated the eventual size of the unit at 2,000 to 4,000 deployment engineers within three years; that headcount, at fully-loaded compensation, supports a multi-billion-dollar annual run rate before any revenue from customer engagements is recognised.

stories.headline: Google Says It Thwarted First Known AI-Built Zero-Day Aimed at Mass Exploitation

key_facts.fact: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) said on May 11, 2026 it had, for the first time, identified a threat actor using a zero-day exploit it believes was developed with help from an AI model, intended for a 'mass exploitation event' that GTIG says it may have disrupted before launch.
key_facts.excerpt: For the first time, GTIG has identified a threat actor using a zero-day exploit that we believe was developed with AI. The criminal threat actor planned to use it in a mass exploitation event but our proactive counter discovery may have prevented its use.

key_facts.fact: The bug was a two-factor authentication bypass in a popular open-source web-based system administration tool, implemented in a Python script that GTIG quietly disclosed and helped patch.
key_facts.excerpt: The bug, a two-factor authentication bypass in a popular open source web-based administration platform, was reportedly developed by criminals working together on a large-scale intrusion operation.

key_facts.fact: Tell-tale signs that an LLM helped write the exploit, per Google, included a 'hallucinated' CVSS score, educational docstrings, and a 'structured, textbook Pythonic format' characteristic of LLM-training data.
key_facts.excerpt: Google's researchers found hints in the Python script used for the exploit that indicated help from AI, like a 'hallucinated CVSS score' and 'structured, textbook' formatting consistent with LLM training data.

key_facts.fact: GTIG ruled out that Gemini was used and did not name which model was used, but said the flaw type — a high-level semantic logic bug — is the kind 'AI systems excel at identifying.'
key_facts.excerpt: Additional evidence suggesting the use of LLM tools in the discovery process is the nature of the flaw - a high-level semantic logic bug that AI systems excel at identifying, rather than memory corruption or input sanitization issues typically uncovered through fuzzing or static analysis.

key_facts.fact: GTIG also flagged that PRC- and DPRK-linked actors are showing 'significant interest' in using AI for vulnerability discovery, and that adversaries are increasingly targeting AI systems themselves, including autonomous skills and third-party data connectors.
key_facts.excerpt: Threat actors associated with the People's Republic of China (PRC) and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) have also demonstrated significant interest in capitalizing on AI for vulnerability discovery.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches 'Daybreak' Cyber-Defense Initiative With GPT-5.5 and Codex Security

key_facts.fact: OpenAI on May 11, 2026 unveiled 'Daybreak,' a cybersecurity initiative pairing frontier OpenAI models with Codex (its agentic harness) and security partners to accelerate cyber defense and 'continuously secure software.'
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI Daybreak is our vision to change the way software is built and defended... Daybreak combines the intelligence of OpenAI models, the extensibility of Codex as an agentic harness, and our partners across the security flywheel to help make the world safer for everyone.

key_facts.fact: Daybreak introduces tiered model access for defenders, including 'GPT-5.5 with Trusted Access for Cyber' for routine defensive workflows and a more permissive 'GPT-5.5-Cyber' tier with stronger verification, gated for authorized red-teaming and penetration-testing.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-5.5 with Trusted Access for Cyber... Most defensive security workflows, including secure code review, vulnerability triage, malware analysis, detection engineering, and patch validation. GPT-5.5-Cyber... Most permissive behavior for specialized authorized workflows, paired with stronger verification and account-level controls.

key_facts.fact: Alongside Daybreak, OpenAI moved Codex Security (formerly Aardvark) into a research preview, rolling out via Codex web to ChatGPT Pro, Enterprise, Business and Edu customers with free usage for the next month.
key_facts.excerpt: Starting today, Codex Security is rolling out in research preview to ChatGPT Pro, Enterprise, Business, and Edu customers via Codex web with free usage for the next month.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says Codex Security cut noise on repeated scans by 84% in one case, reduced over-reported severity findings by more than 90%, and lowered false-positive rates by over 50%.
key_facts.excerpt: scans on the same repositories over time show increasing precision, in one case cutting noise by 84% since initial rollout. We've reduced the rate of findings with over-reported severity by more than 90%, and false positive rates on detections have fallen by more than 50% across all repositories.

stories.headline: OpenAI-Microsoft Revenue Share Capped at $38B vs. $135B Earlier Trajectory

key_facts.fact: OpenAI and Microsoft have agreed to cap total revenue-sharing payments at $38 billion, The Information reported on May 11, 2026, citing a person with knowledge of the arrangement.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI and Microsoft agreed to cap total revenue-sharing payments at $38 billion, U.S. digital news outlet The Information reported on Monday, citing a person with knowledge of the arrangement.

key_facts.fact: Under the prior terms, OpenAI's payments to Microsoft could have totaled roughly $135 billion through 2030 if long-term goals were met; the new cap is part of the partnership amendment unveiled in late April.
key_facts.excerpt: Source: new revenue sharing terms cap OpenAI's payments to Microsoft at $38B; they previously could have totaled $135B through 2030 if long-term goals were met (The Information)

key_facts.fact: Payments will continue through 2030 at the previously agreed 20% rate, independent of any OpenAI declaration of AGI, but now subject to the overall cap.
key_facts.excerpt: revenue share payments from OpenAI to Microsoft will be 'subject to a total cap,' but they will continue through 2030, 'independent of OpenAI's technology progress.'... OpenAI will pay Microsoft at the same percentage, which is 20%.

key_facts.fact: Investors expect the cap to strengthen OpenAI's IPO pitch; some executives have said an offering could come as soon as end-2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The payment cap could help OpenAI present a better financial picture to investors as it works toward a public offering, which some executives said could take place as soon as the end of this year.

key_facts.fact: The April amendment also ended Microsoft's exclusivity and stopped Microsoft's reverse revenue-share payments to OpenAI; Microsoft retains roughly 27% of OpenAI's for-profit arm.
key_facts.excerpt: The revenue sharing is also one way now, so Microsoft no longer has to pay 20 percent of its Azure OpenAI revenue back to OpenAI... Microsoft still owns around 27 percent of OpenAI's for-profit arm.

stories.headline: Helsing Nears $1.2B Round at $18B Valuation, Led by Dragoneer and Lightspeed

key_facts.fact: Munich-based defense-AI startup Helsing is closing in on a roughly $1.2 billion funding round at about an $18 billion valuation, led by US firm Dragoneer Investment Group and co-led by existing investor Lightspeed Venture Partners.
key_facts.excerpt: Five-year-old European military drone startup Helsing is reportedly close to raising a new $1.2 billion round at about an $18 billion valuation. The round is expected to be led by Dragoneer and co-led by existing Helsing investor Lightspeed.

key_facts.fact: The round, first reported by the Financial Times, was 'oversubscribed multiple times' and is at an advanced stage, though timing is not yet finalised.
key_facts.excerpt: The latest Helsing fundraising was oversubscribed multiple times, the FT said. The fundraising plans are at an advanced stage but the timing has not yet been finalised.

key_facts.fact: Helsing's previous round, in June 2025, was a €600 million investment led by Daniel Ek at an estimated €12 billion valuation (~$14 billion).
key_facts.excerpt: Helsing last raised just under a year ago, in June 2025, in a deal that was led by billionaire Spotify founder Daniel Ek. That was a €600 million investment at an estimated €12 billion valuation ($14 billion).

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2021, Helsing started building AI software for defense firms and pivoted to designing drones after Russia's invasion of Ukraine; its AI is designed to be hardware-agnostic and runs on platforms from the Eurofighter Typhoon to autonomous land vehicles.
key_facts.excerpt: The company... develops software platforms that can be used to provide existing hardware with intelligent capabilities... programs for battlefield information in real time, automated [combat] and electronic warfare countermeasures.

stories.headline: Cowboy Space (ex-Aetherflux) Raises $275M Series B at $2B for Orbital AI Data Centers

key_facts.fact: Cowboy Space Corporation, founded in 2024 by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt, announced a $275 million Series B at a $2 billion post-money valuation on May 11, 2026, alongside a rebrand from Aetherflux and a pivot into orbital AI data centers and rockets.
key_facts.excerpt: The company formerly known as Aetherflux has raised a $275M Series B—and has embarked on an ambitious pivot to dramatically expand its space-solar-power business to include orbital data centers and rockets... Aetherflux is rebranding to Cowboy Space Corporation.

key_facts.fact: Index Ventures led the round, with participation from IVP, Blossom Capital, SAIC, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Construct Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, NEA, Interlagos and Bhatt himself.
key_facts.excerpt: The round was led by Index Ventures, with participation from new investors IVP, Blossom Capital and SAIC, alongside existing backers Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Construct Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, NEA, Interlagos and Bhatt himself.

key_facts.fact: Cowboy plans a launch vehicle whose upper stage doubles as a 1-megawatt data center in orbit, replacing the conventional rocket-plus-payload split; first satellite launches this year and first rocket no earlier than end-2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Cowboy Space has designed the rocket's upper stage and data center to be a single vehicle, unlike a traditional rocket that delivers a separate payload to space. Once in orbit, the upper stage will operate as a 1 megawatt data center.

key_facts.fact: The company pitches itself as a response to terrestrial AI compute and energy constraints, with eventual targets of beaming solar power from low-Earth orbit and running inference for 'big model labs' like OpenAI and Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We're standing up our own rocket program,' Baiju Bhatt, the CEO and founder of Cowboy Space Corporation, told TechCrunch. He expects the first launch before the end of 2028.
